body:
# the contributor audit of the completed triangle chord theorem and profile branches



## Triangle Lorentz theorem and scalar closure: PASS

Read all six sections of `candidate 919c51f1d263878e`. Actual normal balance gives the stated column sums. The cyclic signs in g_i=1-d_(i+1)+d_(i+2) are correct. The corner-cap intercept formula gives f_i^2=g_i^2-d_i^2, and the two-vector quadratic identity proves the claimed reverse inequality without an external cone theorem. Applying it with the second signed coordinate reflected gives the precise factor2sqrt(2-g_i). The two-square deficit, its positive denominators, and the equality restrictions are correct. In particular equality forces the other f values equal but does not silently force their cap fractions equal.

The scalar proposition is now fully proved. Summing the three inequalities gives F<=3. The moment and cap ceiling give F>=2/s>59/20. A putative inverse weight at most2/9 gives x<71/100. If another f is at most sqrt(128/119)x, the remaining quadratic inequality makes F<4679/1600, contradicting its lower bound. This supplies the exact coefficient comparison needed in the square-root tangent inequality. The two coordinate increments at c are nonpositive, so the direction of that comparison is correct. The cap-sum constraint then gives the simultaneous inequality2<=rho x+s(f_2+f_3).

The first Lorentz inequality turns this into2<=rho x+2s sqrt(2-x). The derivative sign on the required interval is verified by the displayed rational square comparison. The rational radical upper bounds prove x>67/100 with a strictly positive gap. The reciprocal secant bound then uses the SAME moment identity to bound the other two inverse quantities. The increasing function G is positive at67/100 by an exact rational certificate, contradicting the proposed small weight. There is no unproved symmetry, optimizer, sign of a multiplied numerator, or numerical minimization in this proof.

I independently evaluated all four rational radical-square gaps and the two decisive rational margins. They agree exactly, including2 minus the rational upper bound10269/78125000 and the G lower bound165384/9765625. These computations verify the finite arithmetic already justified by the written inequalities; they do not replace a missing optimization argument.

For the actual triangle corollary, the independently audited incidence theorem supplies one distinct strict vertex per cap. The repeated barycentric proof gives all source coordinates below5/14 and consequently q_i>20/49. The sorted profile implies the weaker cap-sum125/93 exactly. The corner-area/coarea identity identifies the scalar inverse quantities with actual normalized inverse chord lengths. Thus the stated strict2/9 conclusion holds for every actual triangle satisfying the hypotheses. No mixed endpoint-section terms are included in these weights.

## Double-core quadrilateral theorem: PASS

Read `candidate 91fb6de21f312a49` in full. Its two blocks, paired radius perturbation, monotonicity of the untouched block, free-radius perturbation of the other block, and strict objective changes are correct. Both blocks must be singular under the four strict-excess conditions. Positive block null vectors force every Gram slack to vanish and fix all positive-edge charges. Zero edges create no additional vertices. The preserved actual supports then prove uniqueness of the original body, not merely of its polygonal representation. The source explicitly excludes additional core equalities and does not assert a triangle reduction.

## Whole-profile source, Sections6--8: PASS

Read the new sections of `candidate 443fb78ca8dd4f80`. Sorting the four roof slopes gives exactly the three listed orders; the two exceptional orders cannot coexist. The cut at zero lies in a middle segment, and the reflected formulas include both peak signs. The coefficient b/4 in the second descending-cell formula is correct. Zero-length pieces are excluded before division or taken by the explicitly justified continuous finite-polygon formulas.

In the two-decreasing-tail branch, threshold feasibility implies a nonpositive sum of mode coordinates. The relaxed quadratic endpoint minimum is a lower bound even if its minimizer falls outside the actual two branches. Relabeling the last roof component is valid; the additional inequalities given for R<1 keep zero before that last segment. The resulting A a+B+C/a bound has the stated coefficients. Positivity on x in[-4/5,4], y>=0 follows from the displayed coefficient estimates, and the discriminant comparison proves the branch inequality without dropping a feasibility condition. Equality requires the identical one-sided profiles. The result covers only that branch until Section8 is used.

For Section8, the fixed first-peak section contributes a contained middle roof. The disjoint triangle from the first fall and the second upper support point supplies the additional area. The calculation gives exactly R(2-q)/6+(p+1)/12+F_B((1-2p)/3)/4. Tail monotonicity and the centroid-cap contraction give the stated weaker bound. The contraction factor is nonnegative and at least1-1/R. One endpoint threshold is always nonpositive, so at least4/9 is paid by the two endpoints together. The final bound is increasing for R>=1 and exceeds4/3 at9/2 by17/1458. The overlap of the wide-ratio range and the two-decreasing-tail range is valid after either endpoint relabeling.

The remaining compact-range mixed-tail and support-transition cases are not proved by these sections. No all-tent or all-dimensional functional conclusion is inferred.

## Subsequent quantitative margin and narrower-increasing branch: PASS

Read Section7 of the triangle Lorentz source. Replacing the putative inverse-weight bound by223/1000 still forces x<71/100 by its exact square comparison. Every intervening tangent and reciprocal estimate is unchanged. The coefficient1554/223, the positive lower coefficient of m at x=67/100, and the rational lower bound975345521/278750000000 have the correct signs and values. The final reciprocal comparison gives the claimed strict223/1000 ordinary bound. Its difference from2/9 is7/9000. No automatic transfer to mixed weights is claimed.

Read Section9 of the whole-profile source. For an increasing branch of width1 and decreasing branch of widthR>=1, the stationary formula gives t<1 and T>0. The support and mode inequalities reduce as stated and force R<2. The formulas for the two reflected roof cells agree with the earlier exact roof calculation. Inside each cell the total is concave in a, using the proved quadratic-over-positive-affine convexity identity. At fixed R,t the only endpoints are a=1, T=0, and the two roof-order boundaries; all other geometric bounds are either automatic or included in those endpoints.

On each roof-order boundary, the substituted total is again concave in a. The actual feasible intervals, when nonempty, run from a T=0 limit to a=1. The displayed lower endpoints at t=1 have nonpositive T. The possibly singular R=1,t=1 corner has a vanishing endpoint loss uniformly in a and is safe. Thus this is a valid finite boundary reduction rather than an unsupported inference from local concavity.

At a=1 the two numerator polynomials have the stated positive lower certificates. The first uses the negative cubic term with y<=1 and the positive linear term with y>=x^2, in the correct directions. The second uses its decreasing quadratic B on0<=y<=1-2x-x^2 and the explicit B(U) bound. Both are strictly positive on the open branch. Supporting and mode transitions are accounted for: two increasing pieces cannot minimize in their interior; a full endpoint pays at least1; an empty transition against a proper positive-density tail has nonzero derivative; mode minima adjoining decreasing pieces are already in the closed two-decreasing branch. Facet endpoints follow by continuity of the finite polygon and tail formulas. The wider-increasing branch remains separate and unproved by Section9.

## Wider-increasing branch with nonnegative middle peak: PASS

Read Section10 of the same profile source. At fixed0<R<1, the constraints define the stated compact polygon. The inequality D>= (1-R)/2 keeps the endpoint denominator positive. In the reflected-cap cell using R^2-V as a denominator, V=R^2 would require a=0 and is infeasible; the alternative cell uses the strictly positive denominator a. Thus there is no hidden singular division at its boundary.

The joint perspective-concavity proof applies separately on each roof-order cell. The entire a=1 boundary is covered by concavity of its numerator in y and the two strictly positive endpoint values, with positive denominators. The T=3D boundary is a closed two-decreasing-tail case. On H=0, the two own-cap formulas are affine and the endpoint term is concave in a; the listed endpoints and breakpoint exhaust that edge, and all their displayed positivity estimates hold.

The remaining cell vertices must lie on V=0 or V=R^2 and one internal roof line. Aside from previously covered or infeasible endpoints, these are exactly C_0 and C_1. Their feasibility restrictions have the correct direction. At C_0 convexity of the negative-valued quartic between its endpoints proves negativity throughout. At C_1 the denominator is positive and every listed Bernstein coefficient is positive. Consequently every cell vertex has the required bound, and joint concavity proves the entire nonnegative-peak branch. The negative-peak branch has not been inferred from this argument.
